summary.text: Jason Belton of Blythewood, a Democrat and vice president of the Greater Columbia Central Labor Council, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Secretary of State of South Carolina to Republican incumbent Mark Hammond.

A labor official and small-business co-owner who was formerly operations director for the South Carolina American Federation of Labor, he listed voter rights and fair elections and workers' rights as his top issues.

paragraphs.text: Belton, 39, is married and has four children, according to the campaign information published by SC Now.
He is vice president of the Greater Columbia Central Labor Council, which works with the AFL-CIO to represent the interests of local unions.
His other listed experience includes co-founding Vision Walkers, co-owning Belton Does It Best and serving as financial officer for C&J Consulting LLC.
Belton won the Democratic nomination by defeating Edwina Winter in the June 2026 primary.
SC Now noted that he did not respond to its request for information, so the details it published come from his campaign website.
He received 47% of the vote to Mark Hammond's 53%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
